item.title: Christa Pike Discharged From Hospital After Surviving Execution Attempt
item.author: Emily Cochrane
item.content:encoded: Ms. Pike, 50 and convicted of the 1995 murder of a classmate, survived two doses of the drug pentobarbital late last month.

item.title: Exasperation and Resignation in Greece Over Allegations Against Kimberly Guilfoyle
item.author: Niki Kitsantonis, Lara Jakes and Lynsey Chutel
item.content:encoded: The U.S. ambassador to Greece is facing accusations that she asked a donor to pay off her credit card bill before she took up her post in Athens.

item.title: Trump Suggests Ukraine Needs a New President, Blasting Zelenskyy
item.author: Catherine Lucey
item.content:encoded: President Donald Trump demanded that Volodymyr Zelenskyy halt attacks on Russian oil refineries and suggested he should consider stepping aside as Ukraine’s president, escalating a fight centered on securing more diesel supplies for the US ahead of the midterm elections.

item.title: More Than 500 Trees to Be Cut Down at D.C. Golf Course That Trump Wants to Redo
item.author: Luke Broadwater
item.content:encoded: The National Park Service notified a court of the plan as part of continuing litigation over the president’s proposal to create a “champion-level” course.

item.title: Saudi Arabia Suspends Riyadh Airport Operations After Attack
item.author: Sara Gharaibeh and Kateryna Kadabashy
item.content:encoded: Saudi Arabia said it temporarily suspended operations at the Riyadh airport Saturday after an “enemy” attack as air traffic was disrupted for the third time this week amid an intensifying conflict with Yemen’s Houthis.

item.title: After Christa Pike’s Botched Execution, Tennessee’s Lethal Injection Protocol Draws Scrutiny
item.author: Emily Cochrane
item.content:encoded: The differences between the current protocol and the previous one have become a focus in Christa Pike’s failed execution.

item.title: Trump Turns to Russia as Diesel Prices Rise
item.content:encoded: Bloomberg Congressional Reporter Caitlin Reilly and ABC News State Department Reporter Shannon Kingston join hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini on Bloomberg This Weekend to discuss President Donald Trump's agreement to obtain Russian diesel as rising energy costs put pressure on Republicans ahead of the midterm elections. They examine Ukraine's objections to the deal, disagreements over tariffs and the Iran war in competitive Senate races, and Secretary of State Marco Rubio's foreign policy agenda amid allegations involving the US ambassador to Greece. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Supreme Court Recusals in Spotlight as Alito Drops From Oil Case
item.author: Greg Stohr
item.content:encoded: Justice Samuel Alito’s decision not to take part in a major climate-change case because of his wife’s stock holdings is putting renewed focus on the US Supreme Court’s recusal practices as it kicks off its new nine-month term.

item.title: Trump Hypes Megaprojects to Voters Who Lament Gas, Food Costs
item.author: Jennifer A. Dlouhy and Josh Wingrove
item.content:encoded: Presidents have long made bombastic pledges to voters in last-minute electoral appeals.

item.title: Cockroach Party Leaders Detained to Stop Protests
item.content:encoded: Indian authorities detained Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke and spokespersons Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka ahead of a planned demonstration against a contentious revision of voter rolls. Police imposed sweeping restrictions in the national capital to stop supporters and allies from gathering for the youth-led protest. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: EU Plans Measures to Halve Imports of Chinese Hybrid Cars
item.author: Donato Paolo Mancini, Jenny Leonard and Alberto Nardelli
item.content:encoded: The European Union intends to use safeguard measures to cut the number of hybrid car imports from China by half, according to people familiar with the discussions.

item.title: Economic Pain and an Unpopular Trump Put G.O.P. on its Heels With Three Weeks to Go
item.author: Patricia Mazzei and Shane Goldmacher
item.content:encoded: Inflation has hurt Americans at many levels: Farmers, truckers, consumers. It has also expanded the electoral map into what was safely Republican country just a few months ago.

item.title: EU Eyes €160 Billion Cut to Proposed Budget Heading to Talks
item.author: Suzanne Lynch
item.content:encoded: European Union leaders will discuss a scaled back budget when they meet in Brussels next week after negotiators slashed the initial proposal in response to pressure from some countries.

item.title: Fact-Checking Senate Ads in Iowa, New Hampshire and North Carolina
item.author: Linda Qiu
item.content:encoded: We assess three campaign ads in the battleground states that have focused on the cost of living.

item.title: Burnham’s Senior Officials Are Trading Blame Over Economic Pain
item.author: Alex Wickham
item.content:encoded: Andy Burnham ended a barnstorming speech at his party conference last week by pledging to restore a spirit of unity to the country. By the time he walked off stage he seemed to have succeeded in something much harder: restoring unity to his own party.

item.title: For Trump, a Firing Squad on Livestream Becomes the Latest Spectacle
item.author: Peter Baker
item.content:encoded: The idea seemed to surprise even some inside the Trump administration.

item.title: India Police Detain Protesters, Lock Down Delhi Over Voter Rolls
item.author: Rajesh Roy, Atul Dev and Asmi Bhatia
item.content:encoded: Police in India’s capital cracked down on protests against a contentious review of voter rolls, detaining youth leaders and locking down central New Delhi with thousands of security personnel.

item.title: Trump Says He Will Import Russian Diesel Fuel Amid High Prices
item.author: Chris Cameron, Ivan Penn and Valerie Hopkins
item.content:encoded: President Trump said Russia had agreed to ship potentially millions of tons of diesel fuel in the coming months. But the amounts would be small relative to global demand.

item.title: F.B.I. Arrests Key Suspect in ShinyHunters Hack of Its Own Agents’ Data
item.author: Devlin Barrett and Dustin Volz
item.content:encoded: The hack left the nation’s premier law enforcement agency racing to respond as both the victim and the investigator of a murky group that threatened to expose agents’ personal information.

item.title: Trump Warns Norway He Won’t Forget Nobel Peace Prize Snub
item.author: Jennifer A. Dlouhy and Catherine Lucey
item.content:encoded: President Donald Trump fumed at the Norwegian committee that awards the Nobel Peace Prize, saying that the fact it didn’t go to him “is just another sign of how Norway and all these others are ripping off our country.”

item.title: Senate Fact Finders Decry Costs of Immigrant Detention at Guantánamo
item.author: Carol Rosenberg
item.content:encoded: The setup has cost more than $100 million, the study said. A recent inspection found nearly 450 government employees and zero detainees.

item.title: Charlamagne Tha God on Netflix Deal, Midterm Elections, Mental Health
item.content:encoded: Charlamagne Tha God joins Bloomberg's Romaine Bostick to talk about the world of podcasting, the "Breakfast Club" partnership on Netflix, midterm elections and much more. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Donor Says Kimberly Guilfoyle Sought Money From Him to Cover Debt
item.author: Sharon LaFraniere
item.content:encoded: Correspondence suggests that Ms. Guilfoyle, the U.S. ambassador to Greece and former fiancée of Donald Trump Jr., asked a G.O.P. donor to pay off her credit card.

item.title: In Deep-Red Kansas, a Surprisingly Competitive Senate Race Takes Shape
item.author: Jess Bidgood
item.content:encoded: Adam Hamilton wants to be the first Democrat to win a Senate seat there in nearly 100 years.

item.title: Trump: Putin To Release Diesel Into Global Market
item.content:encoded: "Balance of Power" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Rep. Debbie Wasserman Schultz (D-FL) says President Trump’s deal with Russia to release diesel supplies is a “desperate political move” designed to help Republicans ahead of the midterms and argues he cares more about his party’s political outcome than addressing the cost of living. Robert Post, professor and former dean at Yale Law School, says allowing the Trump administration to decide which members of the press can access the White House could “deform the press coverage of the president” and leave the public without complete coverage. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Bessent Will Likely Cut US Long Bond Sales Next Month, Says Citi
item.author: Greg Ritchie
item.content:encoded: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent is likely to reduce the auction sizes for long-dated government bonds — and could even cancel sales of 20-year debt altogether, according to Citigroup Inc.

item.title: DOJ Scrutinizes Binance Compliance With 2023 Settlement Deal
item.author: Chris Strohm
item.content:encoded: The US Justice Department is scrutinizing whether Binance Holdings Ltd. breached a landmark settlement with the US government, as authorities probe activity on the platform for potential Iran sanctions violations.

item.title: Post Says White House Press Limits Could ‘Deform’ Coverage
item.content:encoded: Robert Post, professor and former dean at Yale Law School, says allowing the Trump administration to decide which members of the press can access the White House could “deform the press coverage of the president” and leave the public without complete coverage. Post says the broader conflict between the administration and the courts is a difficult one because courts rely on the executive branch’s good-faith compliance to enforce their orders. He speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Top Democratic Group Pumps Millions Into Kansas Senate Race
item.author: Bayliss Wagner
item.content:encoded: The $5 million investment from the main super PAC for Senate Democrats is a sign that party leaders see a path to winning in another red state as the political environment worsens for Republicans.

item.title: Katie Zacharia Picked as Trump’s New White House Press Secretary
item.author: Hamed Aleaziz, Tyler Pager and Karoun Demirjian
item.content:encoded: Ms. Zacharia is a conservative commentator who is also an adviser to the company that runs President Trump’s social media site, Truth Social. She succeeds Karoline Leavitt.

item.title: Fort Hood Shooter’s Execution Could Face Challenge in Federal Courts
item.author: Abbie VanSickle and John Ismay
item.content:encoded: Legal experts say the former Army officer convicted in a 2009 mass shooting could face a narrow, rushed path to appeal a public execution by firing squad.

item.title: Trump Casts Himself as Columbus’s Protector in Pitch to Italian Americans
item.author: Jonathan Swan
item.content:encoded: President Trump sought to inject the Genoese explorer into the current political conversation.

item.title: Kansas Senate Race Is a Surprising New Midterm Fight
item.author: Jess Bidgood
item.content:encoded: Republicans are suddenly racing to defend a seat in Kansas, where Democrats are trying to win a Senate race for the first time in nearly a century.

item.title: Some G.O.P. Lawmakers Pan Hegseth’s Plan to Stream Execution of Fort Hood Shooter
item.author: Robert Jimison
item.content:encoded: Some G.O.P. members of Congress said that broadcasting the execution of the Fort Hood shooter was inappropriate, though others gleefully applauded it.

item.title: Vance Says He Would Not Watch Livestreamed Execution of Fort Hood Shooter
item.author: Chris Cameron
item.content:encoded: The vice president also cast doubt on whether the public execution of Maj. Nidal Malik Hasan, the 2009 Fort Hood gunman, would go forward as Pentagon officials have planned.

item.title: Trump Says Putin to Supply US With Diesel Ahead of Midterms
item.author: Catherine Lucey, Jennifer A. Dlouhy and Will Kubzansky
item.content:encoded: President Donald Trump is working with Vladimir Putin to release Russian diesel supplies into global markets, a move that upends years of sanctions as the White House seeks ways to tame soaring fuel prices ahead of the US midterm election.

item.title: Trump Administration Hits International Criminal Court With Severe Sanctions
item.author: Edward Wong and Jeanna Smialek
item.content:encoded: U.S. officials announced the new, sweeping punishments just hours after the Nobel Peace Prize committee gave its annual honor to a former court judge.

item.title: EU Says China Will Cut Hybrid Car Exports by Millions
item.author: Linda Lew and Jorge Valero
item.content:encoded: The European Union said China agreed to slash millions of hybrid car exports to the bloc, pointing to a potential trade detente before EU leaders meet next week to discuss further steps against Beijing.

item.title: India Slams Vance for ‘Offensive’ Remarks on Foreign Workers
item.author: Sudhi Ranjan Sen
item.content:encoded: India’s government criticized Vice President JD Vance for “deeply offensive” remarks in which he referred to foreign recruits at software firms in the US, many of whom are Indians, as servants.

item.title: New Delhi Deploys Heavy Security Ahead of Voter-Roll Protest
item.author: Rajesh Roy and Sudhi Ranjan Sen
item.content:encoded: From mass detentions to liquor-store closures, authorities in New Delhi are leaving little to chance as they prepare for a weekend of protests over a contentious revision of India’s voter rolls.
